newsitem.title: INDIA: India Siel, Austria's Plansee in venture.
newsitem.headline: India Siel, Austria's Plansee in venture.

text.p: India's Siel Ltd said on Monday it launched a joint venture involving an equal partnership with Austria's Plansee TIZIT GmbH to make cutting tools for use in engineering industries.

Siel's chairman, Siddharth Shriram, told a news conference in the Indian capital that Siel had sold to Plansee 50 percent stakes in its subsidiary, India Hard Metals, which has been renamed Siel TIZIT Ltd.

"Machinery has all been imported and the product so far produced in Calcutta with Plansee TIZIT technology is by far superior to any product produced by similar companies in India," Siel said in a statement.

The new company, which has a share capital of 300 million rupees ($8.4 million), would eventually have sales of an equivalent amount at full capacity, Shriram said. The firm has received the necessary government approvals, he said.
Customer trials had shown that Plansee's products offered a 30 percent cost reduction to users, Shriram said.
With its products, the joint venture expects to break into a league with Sandvik Asia and Widia India, Shriram said.
"We feel that we are one of the big boys in the business in India," he said.
"A great demand from automobile, railways, machine tool engineering, forming and mining industries is on the way,"the statement said.

Michael Schwarzkopf, president of family-owned Plansee TIZIT, said the relevant segment of the Indian tool market had total annual sales of around $80 million. Plansee TIZIT has an annual sales turnover of around $410 million.
